concepts.name: Database
concepts.description: A database is an organized collection of structured data. In the context of SQL (Structured Query Language), we're typically referring to relational databases, which store data in tables with predefined relationships between them.

components.name: Database
components.description: Logical container for organized collection of structured data

components.name: Schema
components.description: Logical grouping of database objects (tables, views, stored procedures)

components.name: Table
components.description: Collection of related data entries consisting of rows and columns

components.name: Row/Record
components.description: Single data entry in a table (e.g., information about one person)

components.name: Primary Key
components.description: Unique identifier for each record (ensures uniqueness)

components.name: Foreign Key
components.description: Field that links to a primary key in another table (creates relationships)

types.name: DECIMAL/NUMERIC
types.description: Exact decimal numbers with fixed precision (e.g., 10.5, 3.14159)

types.name: FLOAT/DOUBLE
types.description: Approximate decimal numbers (better for calculations where precision isn't critical)

examples.code: SELECT * FROM table_name ORDER BY column_name;
INSERT INTO table_name (column1, column2) VALUES (value1, value2);

INSERT INTO table_name (column1, column2) 
VALUES (value1, value2), (value3, value4);
UPDATE table_name SET column1 = value1 WHERE condition;

types.name: INNER JOIN
types.description: Returns records that have matching values in both tables
types.example: SELECT * FROM table1 INNER JOIN table2 ON table1.id = table2.id;

types.name: LEFT JOIN
types.description: Returns all records from the left table and matched records from the right table
types.example: SELECT * FROM table1 LEFT JOIN table2 ON table1.id = table2.id;

types.name: RIGHT JOIN
types.description: Returns all records from the right table and matched records from the left table
types.example: SELECT * FROM table1 RIGHT JOIN table2 ON table1.id = table2.id;

types.name: FULL OUTER JOIN
types.description: Returns all records when there is a match in either left or right table
types.example: SELECT * FROM table1 FULL OUTER JOIN table2 ON table1.id = table2.id;

functions.name: SUM
functions.description: Returns the sum of values in a column

functions.name: AVG
functions.description: Returns the average of values in a column

functions.name: MAX/MIN
functions.description: Returns the maximum or minimum value in a column

features.name: GROUP BY
features.description: Groups rows that have the same values into summary rows
features.example: SELECT column1, COUNT(*) FROM table_name GROUP BY column1;

features.name: HAVING
features.description: Specifies conditions for grouped rows (similar to WHERE but for groups)
features.example: SELECT column1, COUNT(*) FROM table_name GROUP BY column1 HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;

features.name: Subqueries
features.description: A query nested inside another query

types.name: Single row subquery
types.example:
SELECT * FROM table1 
WHERE column1 > (SELECT AVG(column1) FROM table1);

types.name: Multiple row subquery
types.example:
SELECT * FROM table1 
WHERE column1 IN (SELECT column1 FROM table2);

techniques.name: Indexing
techniques.description: Indexes improve query performance by allowing the database to find and retrieve specific rows much faster
best_practices: Index columns used in WHERE clauses
Avoid over-indexing (indexes consume storage and slow down writes)

techniques.name: Query Optimization
techniques: Use specific column names instead of `SELECT *`
Use appropriate WHERE clauses to limit data retrieval
Optimize JOIN operations (join on indexed columns)
Use EXPLAIN to analyze query performance
techniques.example: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = 'user@example.com';

properties.name: Atomicity
properties.description: Ensures that all operations in a transaction complete successfully; if any operation fails, the entire transaction is rolled back

properties.name: Consistency
properties.description: Ensures that the database properly changes states upon a successfully committed transaction

properties.name: Isolation
properties.description: Ensures that concurrent transactions don't interfere with each other

properties.name: Durability
properties.description: Ensures that once a transaction is committed, it will remain so, even in the event of a system failure

concepts.name: Transaction Control

when_to_use_sql: When data structure is consistent and well-defined
When relationships between data entities are important
when_to_use_nosql: When dealing with large volumes of unstructured data
For applications where high performance and availability are more important than consistency

practices.name: Normalization
practices.description: The process of organizing database tables to reduce data redundancy and improve data integrity

forms.name: First Normal Form (1NF)
forms.description: Eliminate duplicate columns and create separate tables for related data

forms.name: Second Normal Form (2NF)
forms.description: Meet 1NF requirements and ensure all non-key attributes are fully dependent on the primary key

forms.name: Third Normal Form (3NF)
forms.description: Meet 2NF requirements and remove columns not dependent on the key

practices.name: Entity-Relationship Modeling
steps: Define cardinality of relationships (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many)

questions.question: What is the difference between DELETE and TRUNCATE statements?
answer: DELETE: DML command that removes specified rows, can be rolled back, slower
TRUNCATE: DDL command that removes all rows, cannot be rolled back, faster

questions.question: What are SQL constraints?
answer: NOT NULL: Ensures column cannot have NULL value
UNIQUE: Ensures all values in column are different
PRIMARY KEY: Uniquely identifies each record
FOREIGN KEY: Links tables together
CHECK: Ensures values meet specified condition
DEFAULT: Sets default value for column

questions.question: Explain the difference between UNION and UNION ALL
answer: UNION: Combines result sets and removes duplicates
UNION ALL: Combines result sets but keeps duplicates (faster)

questions.question: What is a database index and how does it work?
answer: Speeds up data retrieval but slows data modification
Similar to a book index - points to where data is stored
Trade-off between read and write performance

questions.question: What is a correlated subquery?
answer: A subquery that references columns from the outer query
Executed once for each row processed by the outer query

questions.question: How do you eliminate duplicate rows in a query result?
questions.answer: Use DISTINCT keyword: `SELECT DISTINCT column FROM table`

questions.question: What is a self-join?
answer: Joining a table to itself by treating it as two tables
Used when a table contains hierarchical or related data within itself

questions.question: Explain the difference between WHERE and HAVING clauses
answer: WHERE: Filters rows before grouping
HAVING: Filters groups after grouping

questions.question: What is a view in SQL?
answer: Virtual table based on result of SELECT query
Does not store data physically
Can simplify complex queries

questions.question: What is the purpose of the COALESCE function?
answer: Returns the first non-NULL expression from a list
Useful for handling NULL values
Example: `SELECT COALESCE(column1, column2, 'N/A') FROM table`

topics.title: CAP Theorem and Database Systems
topics.description: The CAP theorem states that a distributed database system can only guarantee two of the following three properties simultaneously:

properties.name: Consistency
properties.description: All nodes see the same data at the same time

properties.name: Availability
properties.description: Every request receives a response, without guarantee that it contains the most recent data

properties.name: Partition Tolerance
properties.description: The system continues to operate despite network partitions

topics.implementation: Most SQL databases prioritize Consistency and Availability (CA), while many NoSQL solutions choose Availability and Partition Tolerance (AP) or Consistency and Partition Tolerance (CP).

oltp.name: OLTP (Online Transaction Processing)
characteristics: Characterized by many short, simple transactions
Example: Processing customer orders, banking transactions

olap.name: OLAP (Online Analytical Processing)
characteristics: Used for business intelligence and data analysis
Characterized by complex queries on large amounts of data
Example: Sales analysis, financial reporting, forecasting

types.name: DDL (Data Definition Language)
types.description: Commands that define the structure of database objects

types.name: DML (Data Manipulation Language)
types.description: Commands that manipulate data within objects

types.name: DCL (Data Control Language)
types.description: Commands that control access to data

topics.name: Window Functions
topics.description: Window functions perform calculations across a set of rows related to the current row
topics.example:
SELECT 
    employee_name,
    department,
    salary,
    AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department) as dept_avg_salary
FROM employees;

topics.name: Common Table Expressions (CTEs)
topics.example:
WITH employee_stats AS (
    SELECT department, AVG(salary) as avg_salary
    FROM employees
    GROUP BY department
)
SELECT e.employee_name, e.department, e.salary, es.avg_salary
FROM employees e
JOIN employee_stats es ON e.department = es.department;
